source_item.title: Customers are chasing higher-rate products. That’s bad news for banks like HSBC.
source_item.summary: Shares of banking giant HSBC Holdings fell as much as 7% on Tuesday as the lender revealed that customers are increasingly turning to higher-rate products.

card.plain_headline: Banks face pressure as customers seek higher rates
card.what_happened: Banks like HSBC are seeing their shares fall because customers are moving their money into higher-interest-paying products. This trend reduces the banks' profit margins on loans and deposits.
card.what_happened_verbose: Major banks are experiencing a shift in customer behavior where depositors are actively seeking out financial products that offer higher interest rates. This migration of funds from lower-yield accounts to higher-yield alternatives puts pressure on banks' net interest margins (NIM), which is the difference between the interest income they generate and the interest they pay out. For banks with a significant portion of their business in regions with competitive deposit rates or those heavily reliant on traditional deposit funding, this trend can lead to reduced profitability and stock price declines.
